page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.12xlarge is a storage-optimized seventh-generation instance powered by a 24-core, 48-thread Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 384 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, offering 8 GB per vCPU, alongside a local storage configuration of 30,000 GB across high-performance NVMe SSDs. Network throughput reaches a baseline speed of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong memory bandwidth and execution efficiency, with small-block cached memory reads achieving 4105.8 GB/sec and uncached memory reads reaching 224.54 GB/sec. CPU instruction capabilities include Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, enabling top-tier LLM inference speed on lightweight models, such as 337.92 tokens per second on a 135M model. Database and key-value workloads achieve 26,466.5 PassMark database operations per second and 71.48 million Redis SET operations per second, supported by 320 MB of L3 cache.

The combination of 30 TB local NVMe storage and high memory density per vCPU provides high resource consolidation for data-intensive applications. However, the instance lacks dedicated GPU hardware, placing heavy multi-billion-parameter LLM generation performance at lower tiers compared to hardware-accelerated nodes. The i7ie.12xlarge is designed for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, real-time analytics, high-throughput key-value stores, and data-heavy enterprise software compilation.
description: Amazon Web Services i7ie.12xlarge is a storage-optimized instance equipped with 48 vCPUs from a 24-core Intel Xeon 8559C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz, 384 GB of DDR5 memory, and 30,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with 50 Gbps baseline networking, it delivers high memory and storage density. Hardware features including AMX and AVX-512 instructions support efficient CPU processing, reflected in high Redis throughput of 71.48 million SET operations per second and small-model LLM inference rates. With 8 GB of RAM per vCPU and extensive NVMe capacity, the instance offers cost-efficient scaling for storage-heavy workloads without requiring external block devices. The lack of discrete GPUs limits multi-billion parameter model execution speeds. This instance is suited for high-density transactional databases, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caches, and data-intensive batch processing.
